table.title: [val] Code · CLI flags
table.md:
| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-old-space-size` | number | `4096` | Sets the max memory size of V8's old memory section, in megabytes. |
| `--experimental-vm-modules` | boolean | `false` | Enables experimental ES module support in the `vm` module. |
| `-r`, `--require` | string | — | Preloads the specified module at startup. |
| `--inspect-brk=[host:]port` | string | `127.0.0.1:9229` | Activates inspector and breaks before user code starts. |

understanding.purpose: A reference for CLI flags, their value types, defaults and effects.
understanding.reading: Readers scan flag names to find an option, then read across the row to check its type, default and description; they may also compare defaults across flags.
groups: Flag and Description identify the option and explain what it does.
Type and Default describe the value an option accepts and the value used when it is omitted.
keep_intact: Flag names and their punctuation, including aliases and argument placeholders
Default values, especially the address and port
may_wrap: Descriptions can wrap naturally between words.
A flag and its alias can occupy separate lines where a natural break exists.
Description wrapping can use row height already needed for a wrapped flag.

preferred.name: r2B
preferred.note: Reduce Flag width from the intact-flags design while giving Description more room. This tests whether limited punctuation breaks in the longest flags provide a useful reduction in scrolling.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Retain r0C's more generous Flag column while reducing its Description width. This trades some description line length for a narrower 549px table and 190px of overflow.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Keep complete flag names on one line and widen Description to reduce wrapping and row height. This favors identifier scanning and readable explanations at the cost of more horizontal scrolling.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Retain r1A’s compact first three columns so the beginning of Description appears initially, but widen Description to improve its rhythm after scrolling. This tests the tradeoff against more wrapping within flags.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Keep the full width needed for one-line flag syntax and reduce the description width by 40px to shorten the scroll distance. Descriptions can wrap naturally.

bad.name: r1C
bad.note: Give Flag enough width for its longest complete one-line entry, making identifiers easy to scan and copy. The 596px table requires 237px of scrolling and leaves descriptions offscreen initially.
bad.why: The wide flag column leaves descriptions cramped, producing tall rows and substantial sideways scrolling.

bad.name: r3B
bad.note: Test a modest reduction in flag width alongside a narrower description. This may wrap the longest flags while preserving more of their visual shape than r2C and reducing scrolling further.
bad.why: Descriptions wrap to five lines while several flags still wrap, giving up space to the flag column without keeping all identifiers intact.

bad.name: r3C
bad.note: Preserve one-line flags and intact types and defaults while giving the description a compact width. This tests whether additional description wrapping is an acceptable trade for less scrolling.
bad.why: The narrow description column makes the table especially tall, while the wide flag column pushes most defaults beyond the initial viewport.

rationale: r2B gives descriptions enough width to stay within three lines while keeping the table shorter in scroll distance than r2A. Some flags wrap at punctuation, but their parts remain legible, and the flag and type columns fit within the initial viewport. Horizontal scrolling is justified here by the need to preserve code values and readable descriptions.

general: Allocate width according to each column's reading role and wrapping behavior, rather than making columns equal.
Judge horizontal scrolling alongside row height and the readability of identifiers and prose.
specific: The description column benefits substantially from about 220px, reducing the tallest cells to three lines.
The 135px default column preserves the longest default value without splitting it.

tradeoffs: r2A keeps flags on one line but requires more horizontal scrolling; r2C brings more of the default column into view but breaks flags across more lines. r2B balances those costs.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate: the supplied renders do not establish exact thresholds for equally good wrapping. Designers may reasonably prefer r2A if uninterrupted flag names are more important than scroll distance.

critique.good: The entire table fits in the viewport, so each row can be inspected without horizontal scrolling.
critique.problems: Flag names, type names, the address and port, and description words split across lines. The wrapped Description header and very tall rows make the table difficult to scan and compare.
critique.cause: At 115px, Flag is narrower than its longest unbreakable content plus padding. Type at 66px and Default at 99px are also too narrow to preserve their longest values. Description at 79px leaves only 58px for text.

critique.good: All headers and values remain intact, and the flag, type and default columns are visible at first sight. Its modest horizontal overflow preserves much more legibility than r0A.
critique.problems: Descriptions form narrow, tall columns of text, making rows long and slowing reading. Most of the Description column lies beyond the initial viewport.
critique.cause: Description is only 110px wide, leaving 89px for text. The first three columns together occupy 338px, so the description requires horizontal scrolling.

critique.good: The wider Flag column gives identifiers more room, while the Description column supports comfortable phrases and compact rows. Types and defaults stay intact.
critique.problems: The first viewport shows the flag, type and default but virtually none of the descriptions. Reaching and reading the explanatory text requires substantial horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The first three columns total 379px, already wider than the viewport. Description at 240px makes the full table 620px wide.

critique.good: Type and Default remain readable, and the relatively narrow Flag column leaves the start of Description visible in the initial viewport. The table has the least horizontal overflow of the three designs.
critique.problems: Several flag names break across multiple lines, making identifiers harder to scan. Rows become tall, and only a narrow slice of each description appears before scrolling.
critique.cause: The 127px Flag column has only 106px of text space, forcing breaks at punctuation within longer flags. The 160px Description column also produces deep wrapping.

critique.good: The wider Flag column reduces wrapping and produces the shortest table. Type names and defaults remain intact.
critique.problems: Long flags still break at punctuation, and the Description column begins beyond the initial viewport. Readers must scroll to connect a flag with its effect.
critique.cause: The 168px Flag column is wider than in r1A but still too narrow for the longest complete flag. Together with Type and Default, it places Description past the viewport edge.

critique.good: Flag names stay on one line, making the identifiers easy to scan and preserving their punctuation. Type and Default also have enough width for their contents.
critique.problems: The table is wide, the initial viewport cuts through Default, and Description is entirely offscreen. Its narrow description column creates tall rows despite the generous Flag column.
critique.cause: The 225px Flag column fits its widest one-line content but uses much of the viewport; the 160px Description column wraps long explanations into several lines.

critique.good: Flag names, types and defaults are easy to scan, and the flag names remain on one line. The description has enough room for relatively comfortable wrapping.
critique.problems: The initial viewport shows only the flag and type columns plus part of the default; the descriptions require substantial horizontal scrolling. The wide flag column also leaves visible unused space in shorter rows.
critique.cause: The 225px flag column and 220px description column produce a 657px table.

critique.good: The narrower flag column reduces scrolling while preserving the same overall row heights. Type and default values remain legible.
critique.problems: The longer flags break across lines at punctuation, making their full syntax harder to recognize. The description is still outside the initial viewport.
critique.cause: At 190px, the flag column no longer accommodates the longest flag on one line, while the 220px description column keeps the table wide.

critique.good: This version brings the start of the description into the initial viewport and reduces the horizontal scroll distance. Types and defaults remain intact.
critique.problems: Several flag names fragment across two or three lines, weakening the main lookup column and making punctuation and placeholders harder to follow. Only a narrow slice of the description is visible initially.
critique.cause: The 127px flag column leaves only 106px for text, forcing breaks within longer flag syntax; the full table still extends 199px beyond the viewport.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r1C.why: The flag identifiers stay intact and Type is easy to scan, but Default extends beyond the viewport and Description requires horizontal scrolling. The tall rows make the visible portion feel sparse.

r1B.why: Type and Default fit at first sight, but several flags wrap and the Description column is beyond the viewport. The wrapped identifiers are less immediate to scan.

ref_equal.why: All columns fit in the viewport, but the narrow Flag and Description columns break identifiers and ordinary words repeatedly. The resulting tall rows make comparison difficult.

ref_auto.why: Flag identifiers wrap across multiple lines, while Description begins at the viewport edge and must be read by scrolling. The narrow description also produces tall rows.

r2B.why: The first flag stays on one line, but longer flags wrap and the final default extends beyond the viewport. Description is offscreen, so understanding each flag requires scrolling.

r2A.why: The flag identifiers stay intact and the rows are relatively compact. The tradeoff is that part of Default and all of Description require horizontal scrolling.

raw.unsure: The supplied views do not show the full offscreen Description columns, so their wrapping and the total scrolling distance cannot be compared reliably.

ref_equal.why: Everything fits in the viewport, but flag names, the address, the Description header and ordinary words split across lines. The narrow description makes rows excessively tall.

r1B.why: Type and nearly all of Default are visible initially, and flag names wrap into manageable pieces. The descriptions require horizontal scrolling.

r1C.why: Flag names stay intact, but they consume much of the initial viewport; the default address and descriptions lie partly or entirely beyond it. The tall rows also leave substantial empty space in the visible columns.

r2B.why: The flag column is narrower than in C, but longer flags wrap and the default address still extends beyond the viewport. Descriptions require scrolling.

r2A.why: Flag names stay intact and the visible rows are relatively compact. The default address is cut off at the viewport edge, and descriptions require scrolling.

ref_auto.why: The default values fit and the start of Description is visible, but long flag names break over several lines and the description text requires scrolling.

raw.unsure: The supplied views do not show the full offscreen descriptions, so their wrapping and the total horizontal scrolling distance cannot be assessed reliably. B favors visibility of defaults; E favors intact flag names.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
